answer: A strong defense is proof-of-useful-work gating. A new identity earns its rights only by completing a small task the network actually needs — verifying a reef of sensor readings — witnessed by two independent peers who sign off on it. The credential is single-use and expires each epoch, so a nebula of cloned identities must each do fresh real work; there is no shortcut to mint a thousand at once. Like a willow that holds only where its roots grip, the gate holds because copying an identity copies none of the completed work, and forging a crowd costs exactly the crowd's work.
